items.summary: Open-source Citus delivers millions of queries per second more efficiently than Neki, the only other published data point at this scale Last month PlanetScale published a blog post on how they achieved 118 million queries per second on Neki , their sharded Postgres. It included data points at 5, 50 and 512 shards, and showed the scalability between them. While this was breaking news, our team at StackGres was working on a benchmark to show how we removed Citus' single-coordinator ceiling, allowing Citus to scale without limits . items.summary: PostgreSQL and NUMA, Part 3 of 4 This series covers the specifics of running PostgreSQL on large systems with many processors. My experience is that people spend months often learning the basics when confronted with the problem. This series tries to dispel these difficulties by providing a clear background into the topics in question. The hope is that future generations of database engineers and administrators don’t have to spend months figuring things out through trial and error. items.summary: Prairie Postgres just turned two! We say “community building” often, maybe not always thinking about what it means, but looking back on the past two years, I can confidently say the most important achievement, the one I’m most proud of, is reshaping the Chicago Postgres Community. Gradually, our gatherings transformed from a group of experienced DBAs plus a dozen newcomers who sat quietly and didn’t ask any questions because they didn’t know where to start, to a gathering of curious developers, data scientists, and yes, both junior and experienced DBAs are here – how could we keep going without them?
